entries.text: notebook: updated Gorrak Vael

You whip your head back and spit the gag clear, and you roar at the shutters for Dreg with everything you have: the book is in the chamber behind the Foreman, break the stair door, don't let them hang Gorrak. To Tessa you shout for the pins in her hair.

You never get to see whether it works. The fight begins in a heartbeat, and you are the slowest man in the room. Tessa's hands are already at the ring in the wall, the pin scraping and slipping in the lock. The grey cloak at your shoulder is quicker than your headbutt. The flat of his sword comes round on a shackled man's easy angle, and the room goes out like a snuffed lamp.

You wake to a quiet you don't trust. It is a little before seven. The shutters stand open, grey light comes in, and the bell has stopped ringing. The wire is cut from your wrists and the iron lies in two halves on the floor. You are lying on the flagstones with someone's cloak folded under your head, and you have 1 hit point.

The ledger-house is full of Tallies. They wear the red-and-tin cloaks, not grey, and they stand along the walls with their spears grounded and no one in front of them. The Foreman sits in his own chair with his wrists bound behind it. His apron is torn, and his soft hands are empty of beads. The barred door to his bedchamber has been broken in, and the iron-bound chest stands on his desk, shut. Nobody has opened it. Tessa kneels beside you with her wrist rubbed raw and a bent hairpin still in her fingers, and she lets out a breath when your eyes open.

"Dreg," she says. "Dreg and the barracks. Twenty spears came up the stair like they'd been waiting years to be asked. The grey cloaks ran for the lower gate." Her voice cracks. "They didn't hang him, Kor."

Gorrak Vael stands at the desk with the bare burned side of his face to the window. Krell leans against the wall behind him with his arm in a sling. In the captain's fist is the Foreman's key chain, and he is looking at it as if it were something that bit him. Dreg, heavy-necked and silent, stands in the doorway with his arms folded. No one speaks. The Foreman watches you with his small, patient eyes.

"The book is in the chest," Gorrak says at last, without turning round. "I have the key. Every man in this room is waiting to see what I do with it, and what you do. You are the one who started this, Emberhide."

You have 1 hit point, no wire on your wrists, and a sister beside you. What does Korvash do?

His father Dargan held the narrow Goat's Throat pass, losing a hand and then his life, so the herd and the children could flee; Korvash swore to him, with his blood on his hands, to protect the weak. input.add_to_description: Day 21 ~6:00 AM: Dreg's revolt in the barracks yard crushed by crossbows. Gorrak and Krell stand under the gate beam with nooses on, hanging stayed until noon.

entries.text: notebook: updated Gorrak Vael

You spit the gag clear and drive your forehead at the grey cloak's face. It lands on his helm, and the helm wins. Your skull rings and he doesn't so much as step back. "Dreg!" you roar at the shutters, "the book's in the chamber behind him! Take the gate-top, don't let them hang Gorrak!" And in Draconic, "Tess, the pins in your hair, now!"

Tessa gets a pin out and into the lock on her wall-ring. It slips, scrapes, and does not turn. The nearest grey cloak hears it, and the Foreman, who has not moved, says only, "Hold her wrist."

The grey cloak you butted does not trouble to curse. He swings his sword flat across your temple, a short, tidy blow, and the room turns white.

The last thing you hear is the dawn bell finishing, and under it a different sound: a hard flat rattle of crossbows from the barracks yard, volley after volley, then a roar that breaks off ragged. Then nothing.

You come up slowly, sick and aching, to a gag in your mouth again and wire biting your wrists. It's a little before ten in the morning. Grey light comes through the cracks of the shutters. You are at 1 hit point.

The yard is quiet. Through the slats you can see a corner of it: a line of Tally-sworn kneeling in irons with crossbows trained on them, and Dreg's thick-necked bulk at the end, bareheaded, blood down one side of his face, staring at the ground. Out on the gate-top walk, the gate beam has two nooses on it, and under them stand Gorrak and Krell, bound, with grey cloaks at their backs. They have not been hanged. A grey cloak is reading something from a slate, and two Tallies are being made to watch.

The Foreman sits at his desk with the shuttered lantern at his elbow, fresh and composed. The scorched ledger's chest is not in sight. Tessa is on her stool with her wrist chained to the ring in the wall, a thin line of blood at her fingers where the pin cut her. She looks at you, and her chin dips once. *Alive.*

"Good morning, Emberhide," the Foreman says pleasantly. "The captain hangs at noon. It is a small thing, and I find it makes a better lesson with an audience. You have two hours to consider the matter of your oath. A little silence will help you think." He nods, and the grey cloak behind you loosens the gag a hair, enough to breathe and not enough to shout.

You are at 1 hit point, gagged, wired to a table leg, with the noon hour ahead. What does Korvash do?

line:
I raise my fist to the slab crews and keep it raised, whispering to Gorrak, "Hold until the file is strung out on the narrow, and not before." I tell Dreg to send two spears to meet the four heading for the Weeping Ledge, quietly, since they'll find it empty and then try to flank us.

When the first torch reaches the tight bend, I drop my fist and roar, "Slabs, now! Slingers, loose!", then step into the road with shield up beside Gorrak to hold the head of the column.

input.add_to_description: Day 40 ~5:35 AM: ambush sprung at the switchback. Slabs crushed five cloaks on the tight bend; a sixth was hurt; sling volleys wounded several more. Roughly fourteen cloaks left, scattered, with Tolk among them. Two Tally spears sent toward the Ledge path against the four flankers. Grunna and Gorrak hold the head of the column in the road. Resolved by hand rulings; Grunna has no tracked sheet.

entries.text: notebook: updated Tolk's Deadline

Before I resolve this, one disclosure. Grunna has no tracked sheet or fight tracker, so I'm rolling this ambush by hand as a ruling. Stat blocks are the hobgoblin I already looked up, and I'll apply the results in the narration.

You keep your fist raised and whisper to Gorrak to wait until the file is strung out on the narrow. You tell Dreg to send two spears quietly after the four heading for the empty Weeping Ledge. Then the first torch reaches the tight bend.

You drop your fist and roar, "Slabs, now! Slingers, loose!"

The bars bite, and the shale shelf lets go. A wall of grey stone slides onto the bend with a sound like a landslide. Five cloaks go under it and do not come out. A sixth is flung against the rock with a broken leg, screaming. Only one of the six leaps clear. Torches roll and gutter in the road.

From the overhang the slings crack. Pebbles and shaped stones hail down, and seven of them find flesh. Cloaks stagger and drop their crossbows, and the file breaks into a knot of shouting men. Some crouch behind the fallen slabs and fire up blind at the overhang. One bolt skitters off the rock beside you.

You step into the road with your shield up beside Gorrak, and the head of the column comes at you out of the smoke and torchlight: five or six grey cloaks, hobgoblins in chain with shields, led by a lean, hard-faced one who carries a rod of tin and a ledger-satchel. That will be Tolk. "Break them," he shouts in Goblin. "The red one's dead, they have only half-blood herders and traitors!" No one listens. They are looking at the slabs.

Behind them, up the goat-path toward the Ledge, you hear steel on steel and a Tally voice shouting. It is half past five and a little more. The road at the bend is ruined, the cloaks are broken but not beaten, and Tolk is thirty paces away with his blade out.

What does Grunna do?
